# Libraries

```{r}
# load libraries
library(FLCore)
library(ggplot2)

library(ggrepel)
library(flextable)

library(EnvCpt)
```

# Data preparation

```{r}
# load object from WGHANSA 2022
load(file.path("..","data","aneq.stk.RData")) # aneq.stk

# remove 2023

aneq.stk <- window(aneq.stk, end=2022)

# recruitment (1st January)
# change units

rec <- rec(aneq.stk)
rec <- rec*1e-6
units(rec) <- "1e9"

# ssb (from FLBiols because it is the same as used in FLBEIA)

aneq.biol <- as(aneq.stk, "FLBiol")
ssb <- ssb(aneq.biol)
# equivalently, (i.e. without fishing mortality)
# quantSums(stock.n(aneq.stk)*exp(-m(aneq.stk)*m.spwn(aneq.stk))*stock.wt(aneq.stk)*mat(aneq.stk))
ssb <- ssb/1000
units(ssb) <- "1000 t"

# create data frame

df <- data.frame(year=as.numeric(dimnames(aneq.stk)$year), 
                 rec=as.numeric(rec), 
                 ssb=as.numeric(ssb))

# create log variables

df <- df %>% 
  mutate(logr=log(rec),
         logssb=log(ssb),
         rat=rec/ssb, 
         lograt=log(rat))

# load data from assessment (same as prepared by Ixak, Almudena and Leire)

sr.dat <- read_excel(file.path("..","data","Procesos_ambientales_anchoa_LI.xlsx"), sheet="R_SSB")

# current Blim (21 000 tonnes)

Blim <- 21

# compare the SSB derived from the FLStock object with the official SSB
# and the R (age0 in numbers) derived from the FLStock object with the official R (age1 in mass)

tmp <- left_join(df, sr.dat, by = c("year" = "Year"))
  
p <- ggplot(tmp, aes(ssb, SSB/1000))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_abline(intercept=0, slope=1, col=2)+
  expand_limits(x=0, y=0)
p

p <- ggplot(tmp, aes(lag(rec), R_age1))+
  geom_point()+
  expand_limits(x=0, y=0)
p

# print data.frame to check data

ft <- flextable(df)
ft

```

# Ricker SR model

```{r}
#Ricker stock-recruitment model 
sr.rick <- FLSR(rec=rec, ssb=ssb)
model(sr.rick) <- "ricker"
sr.rick <- fmle(sr.rick)
c(params(sr.rick))
summary(sr.rick)
plot(sr.rick)
profile(sr.rick, main="Ricker")

# code to check auto-correlation in residuals
res <- c(residuals(sr.rick)) # log(rec(sr.rick)) - log(fitted(sr.rick))
acf(res)
pacf(res)
ar1 <- stats::ar(res, aic=F, order.max=1)
print(ar1)
cbind(rho=ar1$ar, var.pred=ar1$var.pred)
cor(res[- length(res)], res[-1])
ct <- cor.test(res[- length(res)], res[-1])
cbind(rho=ct$estimate, low=ct$conf.int[1], up=ct$conf.int[2], pval=ct$p.value)

# Ricker stock-recruitment model with auto-regressive normal log residuals of first order:

sr.rickAR1 <- FLSR(rec=rec, ssb=ssb)
model(sr.rickAR1) <- "rickerAR1"
sr.rickAR1 <- fmle(sr.rickAR1)
c(params(sr.rickAR1))
summary(sr.rickAR1)
plot(sr.rickAR1)
```

# Beverton-Holt SR model:

```{r}
sr.bh <- FLSR(rec=rec, ssb=ssb)
model(sr.bh) <- "bevholt"
sr.bh <- fmle(sr.bh)
c(params(sr.bh))
summary(sr.bh)
plot(sr.bh)
profile(sr.bh, main="BH")

# code to check auto-correlation in residuals
res <- c(residuals(sr.bh)) 
acf(res)
pacf(res)
ar1 <- stats::ar(res, aic=F, order.max=1)
print(ar1)
cbind(rho=ar1$ar, var.pred=ar1$var.pred)
cor(res[- length(res)], res[-1])
ct <- cor.test(res[- length(res)], res[-1])
cbind(rho=ct$estimate, low=ct$conf.int[1], up=ct$conf.int[2], pval=ct$p.value)

## Beverton-Holt stock-recruitment model with auto-regressive normal log residuals of first order:
# convergence issues

sr.bhAR1 <- FLSR(rec=rec, ssb=ssb)
model(sr.bhAR1) <- "bevholtAR1"
# sr.bhAR1 <- fmle(sr.bhAR1) # It gives NA's. 
# We try other optimization methods: 
sr.bhAR1 <- fmle(sr.bhAR1, method="L-BFGS-B")
c(params(sr.bhAR1))
summary(sr.bhAR1)
plot(sr.bhAR1)

## Beverton-Holt stock-recruitment model (parameterised in terms of steepness and virgin biomass):

sr.bhsv <- FLSR(rec=rec, ssb=ssb)
model(sr.bhsv) <- "bevholtSV"
sr.bhsv <- fmle(sr.bhsv)
c(params(sr.bhsv))
summary(sr.bhsv)
as.numeric(abPars("bevholt", s = params(sr.bhsv)$s, v = params(sr.bhsv)$v, spr0 = params(sr.bhsv)$spr0)) # transformation to a, b parameterization 
c(params(sr.bh)) # the two parameterizations give different results, but it may be due to convergence problems in bhsv model (there are warnings in model fit & strange model plot)
plot(sr.bhsv)
```

# Hockey-Stick SR model 

```{r}
#Hockey-stick (also called segmented regression) stock-recruitment model:
sr.hs <- FLSR(rec=rec, ssb=ssb)
model(sr.hs) <- "segreg"
sr.hs <- fmle(sr.hs)
params(sr.hs) 
# the default method "Nelder-Mead" gives b values within the observed SSB range
# in this case, we don't need to fit again using "SANN" method. For more info on methods, see ?optim
# sr.hs <- fmle(sr.hs, method="SANN")
params(sr.hs) 
summary(sr.hs)
plot(sr.hs)
profile(sr.hs, main="HS")

# code to check auto-correlation in residuals
res <- c(residuals(sr.hs)) 
acf(res)
pacf(res)
ar1 <- stats::ar(res, aic=F, order.max=1)
print(ar1)
cbind(rho=ar1$ar, var.pred=ar1$var.pred)
cor(res[- length(res)], res[-1])
ct <- cor.test(res[- length(res)], res[-1])
cbind(rho=ct$estimate, low=ct$conf.int[1], up=ct$conf.int[2], pval=ct$p.value)

## Hockey-stick with auto-regressive normal log residuals of first order:

sr.hsAR1 <- FLSR(rec=rec, ssb=ssb)
model(sr.hsAR1) <- "segregAR1"
sr.hsAR1 <- fmle(sr.hsAR1)
params(sr.hsAR1)
summary(sr.hsAR1)
plot(sr.hsAR1)

## Hockey-stick stock-recruitment model with the breakpoint fixed at Blim:

sr.hsblim <- FLSR(rec=rec, ssb=ssb)
model(sr.hsblim) <- "segreg"
sr.hsblim <- fmle(sr.hsblim, fixed=list(b=Blim))
params(sr.hsblim)
summary(sr.hsblim)
plot(sr.hsblim)
```

# Geometric Mean SR model 

```{r}
# Geometric mean stock-recruitment model:
sr.gm <- FLSR(rec=rec, ssb=ssb)
model(sr.gm) <- "geomean"
sr.gm <- fmle(sr.gm)
params(sr.gm)
summary(sr.gm)
plot(sr.gm)

# code to check auto-correlation in residuals
res <- c(residuals(sr.gm)) 
acf(res)
pacf(res)
ar1 <- stats::ar(res, aic=F, order.max=1)
print(ar1)
cbind(rho=ar1$ar, var.pred=ar1$var.pred)
cor(res[- length(res)], res[-1])
ct <- cor.test(res[- length(res)], res[-1])
cbind(rho=ct$estimate, low=ct$conf.int[1], up=ct$conf.int[2], pval=ct$p.value)
```

# Quadratic hockey stick SR model 

```{r}
# define quadratic hockey stick (Barrowman and Myers, 2000)

qhs <- function(){
  ## log-likelihood
  logl <- function(a,b,delta,rec,ssb) {
    res<-loglAR1(log(rec), log( ifelse(ssb <= b*(1-delta), 
                                       a*ssb, 
                                       ifelse( ssb < b*(1+delta), 
                                               a*(ssb - ( ssb - b*(1-delta))^2/(4*delta*b)),
                                               a*b))))
    return(res)
  }
  ## initial parameter values
  initial <- structure(function(rec, ssb){
    return(FLPar(a = median(c(rec)/c(ssb), na.rm = TRUE),
                 b = median(c(ssb), na.rm = TRUE),
                 delta = 0.5))},
  lower=c(-Inf, -Inf, 0),
  upper=c(Inf, Inf, 1))
  ## model to be fitted
  model  <- rec ~ ifelse(ssb <= b*(1-delta), 
                         a*ssb, 
                         ifelse( ssb < b*(1+delta), 
                                 a*(ssb - ( ssb - b*(1-delta))^2/(4*delta*b)),
                                 a*b))
  return(list(logl = logl, model = model, initial = initial))}


sr.qhs <- FLSR(rec=rec, ssb=ssb)
model(sr.qhs) <- "qhs"
sr.qhs <- fmle(sr.qhs) # It's not using the bounds
params(sr.qhs)
sr.qhs <- fmle(sr.qhs, method="L-BFGS-B") # specify the method to use the bounds
params(sr.qhs)
summary(sr.qhs)
plot(sr.qhs)
```

# Model comparison 

AIC and BIC values: 

```{r}
# Overall model comparison using AIC and BIC

ft <- data.frame(model=c("ricker","bevholt","segreg","segregBlim","geomean","rickerAR1","bevholtAR1","segregAR1"),
           AIC=sapply(list(sr.rick, sr.bh, sr.hs, sr.hsblim, sr.gm, sr.rickAR1, sr.bhAR1, sr.hsAR1), AIC),
           BIC=sapply(list(sr.rick, sr.bh, sr.hs, sr.hsblim, sr.gm, sr.rickAR1, sr.bhAR1, sr.hsAR1), BIC))
ft <- flextable(ft)
ft
```

Plot of fitted models: 

```{r}
pred.dat <- data.frame(ssb=seq(0, max(df$ssb), length.out=1000))

pred.dat$ricker <- c(params(sr.rick)["a"]) * pred.dat$ssb * exp(-c(params(sr.rick)["b"])*pred.dat$ssb)
pred.dat$bh <- c(params(sr.bh)["a"]) * pred.dat$ssb /( c(params(sr.bh)["b"]) + pred.dat$ssb)
pred.dat$hs <- pmin( c(params(sr.hs)["a"]) * pred.dat$ssb, c(params(sr.hs)["a"]) * c(params(sr.hs)["b"]))
pred.dat$hsblim <- pmin( c(params(sr.hsblim)["a"]) * pred.dat$ssb, c(params(sr.hsblim)["a"]) * Blim)

tmp <- pivot_longer(pred.dat, cols=2:5)

p <- ggplot(tmp, aes(ssb, value))+
  geom_line(aes(col=name))+
  geom_point(data=df, aes(ssb, rec))+
  xlab("SSB")+
  ylab("Recruits (age 0)")
p
```

Coefficients: 

```{r}
ft <- data.frame(rick=c(params(sr.rick)), 
           BH=c(params(sr.bh)),
           HS=c(params(sr.hs)),
           HSBlim=c(params(sr.hsblim)))
ft <- flextable(ft)
ft
```

# Changepoint analysis in Ricker residuals

General analysis using `EnvCpt`:

```{r}
res <- c(residuals(sr.rick)) # log(rec(sr.rick)) - log(fitted(sr.rick))
out <- envcpt(res)
# model comparison by AIC and BIC
AIC(out)
sort(AIC(out))
BIC(out)
sort(BIC(out))

# several plots
plot(out,type='fit') # plots the fits
plot(out,type="aic") # plots the aic values
plot(out,type="bic") # plots the bic values

```

Analysis using `changepoint`:

```{r}
mod <- cpt.meanvar(res, method="PELT") # PELT is fast and exact
plot(mod)
param.est(mod)
cpts(mod)

mod.np <- cpt.np(res, method="PELT")
plot(mod.np)
cpts(mod.np)
```
```{r}
mod <- processStream(res, cpmType = "GLR")  # detect mean and variance changes in Gaussian sequence
mod$changePoints

mod <- processStream(res, cpmType = "Mann-Whitney")  # detect location shifts (non-parametric)
mod$changePoints

mod <- processStream(res, cpmType = "Lepage")  # detect location and/or stream shifts (non-parametric)
mod$changePoints

```

Using strucchange

```{r}
mod <-breakpoints(res ~ 1, breaks = 5) # max number of 5 breaks
summary(mod)
```
